title: Amelia Earhart's Plane Wasn't in the Lagoon. Here's What Was
description:
Amelia Earhart's plane was not the "Taraia Object" in the lagoon of Nikumaroro. On 19 October 2026 (local time) the Archaeological Legacy Institute, Purdue Research Foundation and Purdue University said the shape seen in satellite images since 2015 was most likely a collection of large trees, its shine a carbonate crust, not metal. So what did the expedition find, and where could her plane be?

Part 2 of our Earhart lagoon coverage. Part 1, the case for the lagoon: https://youtu.be/AC0mXDZ7iZs

Free case file for this story (timeline, maps, where the sources disagree, every source): https://earhart.vibewithjudeo.com

This film covers the 17-person expedition, who paid for it (an expected budget of about $900,000, a $500,000 Purdue Research Foundation line of credit, and the 1936 Purdue fund that helped buy the Electra: $40,000, about $0.93 million in 2025 dollars), the five-day voyage from Tarawa, how you identify a plane you can't see (magnetometer, sonar, sub-bottom profiler, probe, dredge), three days stuck on the ship, the result, the 30-inch steel tube, and what is left of the castaway theory.

Notes: "most likely large trees" is the team's own wording. The steel tube had not been identified or linked to the Electra when the team reported. The $900,000 is the institute's expected Phase 1 budget; no final cost was published. The official 1937 finding is that the plane went down at sea near Howland Island. Facts checked 21 October 2026.

title: Nims Purja Is Gone. Here's the Full Story of His Life and Last Climb
description:
On 30 July 2026 an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan killed ten climbers, among them Nirmal "Nims" Purja: the Gurkha from Dana, Nepal, who went from the SBS to Project Possible, the first winter ascent of K2 and Netflix's 14 Peaks. This is the full story, honestly told: the record and the true-summit correction, K2 in winter, the controversies he faced and the allegations he denied, why he was on Broad Peak at all, and the nine climbers who died with him.

A NOTE ON THE FACTS: The 2019 "6 months, 6 days" (189 days) record was later discounted by Guinness after Eberhard Jurgalski's true-summit research (2022) found he stopped short on Dhaulagiri and Manaslu in 2019; he reached both true summits in 2021. His no-oxygen claims (K2 2021, all 14 by 2024, Everest-Lhotse 2026) are his own accounts. title: The Pacific Broke a 1997 Record. Here's What Super El Niño Does Next
description:
A patch of the Pacific at least 3 °C hotter than normal now stretches along the equator over an area roughly the size of the United States, about three times what it was on the same day in 2015. Japan's weather agency says September's El Niño beat its December 1997 record. NOAA's official, warming-adjusted index hasn't broken the record yet, but NOAA gives it an 83% chance between October and December. Here is how El Niño works, how we measure it, who says it's a record (and on which index), what the record-scale El Niños of 1982, 1997 and 2015 did, what this one is already doing, and what the forecasts say comes next.

"Super El Niño" is a nickname, not an official category: NOAA's top category is "very strong". Every forecast in this video is labelled as a forecast. Figures checked 14 October 2026; the next NOAA update is due 12 November 2026.

title: A Former Marine Just Rowed From Peru to Kenya Alone. Here's How He Survived 327 Days
description:
Dave "Dinger" Bell, a 54-year-old former Royal Marine from Dorset, rowed alone from Peru to Kenya: about 28,700 km across the entire Pacific and Indian Oceans, with no support boat, no resupply and not one step ashore. He left La Punta, Callao (Lima) on 9 November 2025 and landed at Kilifi, Kenya on 2 October 2026, 327 days later. This is how he did it: the boat called Billy No Mates, the cyclone season that forced him to slow down, the Coral Sea knockdown, the Indian Ocean gale that flooded his cabin, the two times his emergency beacon went off, and the day he finally touched sand.

He rowed for Rock2Recovery, a UK charity that supports serving personnel, veterans, their families and emergency workers living with stress and PTSD. Donate: https://sportsgiving.co.uk/sponsor/activity/dinger-cross-pacific-and-indian-ocean-row/dinger

A note on the record: his team and much of the press call it the first unsupported row from South America to Africa and the longest unsupported ocean row. As of 15 October 2026 we found no ratification by the Ocean Rowing Society or Guinness World Records. Jacob Adoram's Guinness record for the longest time rowed solo across an ocean (335 days 22 hours) still stands; the comparison in this video is about distance.

title: Vancouver Has Thousands of New Condos Nobody's Bought. Here's Why
description:
Metro Vancouver now has more brand-new, finished condo apartments that nobody has signed to buy than at any time since CMHC began counting in 1990: 4,470 in June 2026, and still 4,248 in August. Two industry estimates value the unsold stock at about $4.4 to $4.6 billion. So why would anyone build thousands of homes in one of the world's most expensive housing markets and leave them sitting there, and why don't developers just cut the price further?

This film looks at the three numbers behind the "$4.5 billion" headline, how Vancouver's presale machine works and why it stalled, what is actually unsold, why lenders can stop price cuts, the June federal–B.C. condo-buying plan and the fight over it, and what each party in B.C.'s Oct 24 election says it would do.

"Unsold" is not the same as "empty": some developers rent units out while they wait. Dollar figures are estimated values, not prices paid. Receiverships mentioned are of project companies, not of any developer as a whole. Claims about the Sanctuary sale come from court filings reported by The Globe and Mail; the parties reportedly settled and none were tested at trial. This video is independent and does not endorse any party. Figures checked 14–15 October 2026.

title: Everest's 'Green Boots' Finally Has a Name. Here's Why He's Still Up There
description:
For thirty years, climbers on Everest's north side passed a small cave at about 8,500 m where a climber from the 1996 storm still lies. They knew him only by his boots. In 2026, India's Indo-Tibetan Border Police named him Lance Naik Dorje Morup, not Tsewang Paljor as most accounts said. The evidence hasn't been made public, his family is still waiting, and the recovery is now expected in spring 2027. This documentary tells the story of the three men from Ladakh, the storm, the cave, and why so many of Everest's dead are still on the mountain.

Out of respect for the dead and their families, this film never shows their remains.

A NOTE ON WHAT IS AND ISN'T KNOWN: India's border police named Dorje Morup in a 2026 recovery tender. How he was identified is disputed: an official told CNN it rests on records, teammates and "technical inputs"; CNN reports Sherpa-collected samples were matched by an Indian lab; another official told the BBC identification was by clothing and gear, with DNA to follow after recovery. No result has been published, and his son says the family was never formally told. Whether the 1996 summit was reached is disputed. Accounts of 11 May 1996 conflict; India's border police accepted the Japanese team's account in June 1996. The cave's position on the maps is approximate; routes are schematic. "About 200 bodies" is a 2015 estimate; no official count exists.

title: Why No One Is Allowed on North Sentinel Island
description:
North Sentinel Island is a square of forest and coral about 50 km west of Port Blair, in India's Andaman Islands. The people who live there, the Sentinelese, have refused contact with outsiders for as long as anyone has records. This documentary tells the real story: the 1880 kidnapping, the 1991 coconut exchange, the 2004 earthquake that lifted their reef out of the sea, the deaths of two fishermen in 2006 and of missionary John Allen Chau in 2018, the American YouTuber arrested in 2025, the law that protects them, and why contact could be deadly. No myths: there is no evidence they are cannibals, and they are not "Stone Age".

A NOTE ON THE NUMBERS: Area 59.67 km² (A&N Forest Statistics; Home Ministry 2017). Census 2011 recorded 15 people and 2001 recorded 39, both counted from boats; India's Home Ministry says the true population "cannot be ascertained" (estimates ~50-150). The protected zone is 5 km of sea from the high-water mark (MHA 2017), not "5 nautical miles". The uplift estimate (1-2 m; at least 30 cm measured) is from Meltzner et al. 2006 / Bilham et al. 2005. title: RJ Mitte Was More Than Walt Jr. Here's the Life He Lived
description:
If you're struggling or thinking about suicide, you are not alone and help is available. In the US, call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline); in Canada, call or text 988 (Suicide Crisis Helpline), any time. In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans: 116 123. Anywhere else, find a free, confidential helpline at https://findahelpline.com. If someone is in immediate danger, call your local emergency number.

RJ Mitte was born with cerebral palsy, and for five seasons he played Walter "Flynn" White Jr., a teenager with cerebral palsy, on Breaking Bad. He died on 12 October 2026, aged 34. This is a tribute to his life: his childhood in Jackson, Mississippi, how he got the role and what it asked of him, his years of disability advocacy, his work after the show, and the people who remember him. It follows media guidelines for reporting on suicide: no details of how he died and no speculation about why. His representatives said he died by suicide; officials had not released an official cause or manner of death when this was published (13 Oct 2026), and an autopsy was ordered.

A public celebration of RJ's life is planned for Friday 16 October 2026 at 10 a.m. at The Mitte Arts and Cultural Center in Brownsville, Texas. His family asks for donations to cerebral palsy research in lieu of flowers (City of Brownsville).

title: The Titanic Is Disappearing. Here's What's Really Left in 2026
description:
In 2024, robots found part of the Titanic's famous bow railing lying on the seabed. This month a video claiming a drone just "entered the Titanic" passed two million views in two days, and the company that holds the salvage rights told a court it could run out of money within six months. So what is really left of the Titanic in 2026, and how long before there's nothing left? Real dive footage, the 2022 digital scan, the bacteria eating the steel, the viral fakes checked against the record, and the court fight over the artifacts.

title: Karl Bushby: Why His Walk Home Took 28 Years
description:
Karl Bushby left Hull in 1998 to walk home from the bottom of South America, with two rules: nothing may move him forward but his own feet, and he can't go home until he walks there. title: They Think Earhart's Plane Is in This Lagoon. Here's Their Evidence
description:
In 1937, Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific. Right now, a Purdue-backed team is sailing to Nikumaroro, a tiny uninhabited atoll in Kiribati, to examine the "Taraia Object" — a shape in the lagoon they think could be her Lockheed Electra. The man who first spotted it now calls it debunked, and TIGHAR says it's a tree. Here's the evidence on both sides, and what happens when they arrive (expected around Oct 12, local time — tentative).

Nothing has been found yet. We'll follow up when the team reports what the object is.

title: How a Glacier Collapse Triggered Nepal's Deadly Flash Flood (It Isn't Over)
description:
A catastrophic glacier collapse in the Himalayas triggered a deadly flash flood that devastated Rasuwa and communities along the Nepal-China border - sweeping away homes, bridges and the Rasuwagadhi border crossing, and leaving hundreds dead and thousands missing.

This documentary explains what happened on August 26, 2026: the ice-rock avalanche above the Lhende valley, the natural dam that failed, the debris flow that followed - and the new barrier lake that burst on August 28, threatening a second flood.
